Facing Difficulty & Hope

phrase: The darkest hour is just before dawn.
meaning: The most difficult moment often comes right before a problem is solved.
example: Just when the team felt hopeless, they scored the winning point — the darkest hour is just before dawn.

phrase: Discretion is the better part of valour.
meaning: It is sometimes better to avoid a dangerous situation than to face it head-on.
example: He decided not to climb the shaky ladder after all — discretion is the better part of valour.

phrase: Crosses are ladders that lead to heaven.
meaning: Suffering and misfortune often reveal the best in a person's character.
example: After breaking her arm, she discovered how patient and brave she could be — crosses are ladders that lead to heaven.

phrase: Every cloud has a silver lining.

example: The rained-out game meant they got to have a cozy movie afternoon instead — every cloud has a silver lining.

phrase: Every rose has its thorn.

phrase: Every path has its puddle.

example: Learning to skateboard meant a few scraped knees along the way — every path has its puddle.

phrase: Death is the great leveller.
meaning: All people are equal when they die.

phrase: Dead men tell no lies.

phrase: The die is cast.

example:

phrase: Elbow grease is the best polish.

phrase: The early bird catches the worm.

phrase: Every man is the architect of his own fortune.

phrase: Constant occupation prevents temptation.

phrase: Don't bite off more than you can chew.

phrase: Don't count your chickens before they're hatched.

phrase: Cross the stream where it is shallowest.

phrase: No cure, no pay.

phrase: Experience is the best teacher.

phrase: Experience is the father of wisdom.

phrase: Enough is as good as a feast.

phrase: Courtesy is contagious.

phrase: (A) friend is like a mirror.

phrase: Friendship is like a circle that never ends.

phrase: Friendship is love with understanding.

phrase: Good accounting makes good friends.

phrase: (A) hedge between keeps friendship green.

phrase: Fine words butter no parsnips.

phrase: (A) good conscience is a soft pillow.

example: She always tells the truth because a good conscience is a soft pillow.

phrase: (A) good name is better than a good face.

phrase: Handsome is what handsome does.

phrase: Hard words break no bones.

phrase: He who digs a pit for others falls into it himself.

phrase: Honesty is the best policy.

phrase: Honey catches more flies than vinegar.

phrase: (A) guilty conscience needs no accuser.

phrase: Gardens are not made by sitting in the shade.

phrase: God helps those who help themselves.

phrase: Great oaks grow from small acorns.

phrase: He can who believes he can.

phrase: He who wills the end wills the means.

Wisdom, Caution & Foolishness

phrase: (A) fool and his money are (soon) easily parted.
meaning: A careless person spends money quickly and without much thought.
example: He spent his whole allowance in a day — a fool and his money are soon parted.

phrase: (A) fool at forty is a fool forever.
meaning: If someone hasn't matured or learned good sense by a certain age, they probably never will.
example: Grandpa laughed and said a fool at forty is a fool forever.

phrase: Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.
meaning: If you're tricked once it's not really your fault, but if it happens again, you should have learned from it.
example: After falling for the same prank twice, he said, 'Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.'

phrase: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.

phrase: Give someone enough rope and they will hang themselves.

phrase: Great minds think alike.

phrase: (A) handful of patience is worth more than a bushel of brains.

phrase: Haste makes waste.

phrase: He who goes slowly goes safely (and goes far).

phrase: He who is everywhere is nowhere.

phrase: He who knows nothing doubts nothing.

phrase: First come, first served.

phrase: Fair exchange is no robbery.

example: They swapped trading cards of equal value — fair exchange is no robbery.

phrase: Familiarity breeds contempt.
meaning: Knowing someone very well over time can sometimes lead to less respect for them.
example: The roommates started bickering over little things — familiarity breeds contempt.

phrase: (A) fly will not get into a closed mouth.

phrase: Forbidden fruit is sweet.

phrase: (A) growing youth has a wolf in his belly.

phrase: (A) happy heart is better than a full purse.

phrase: (A) heavy purse gives to a light heart.

phrase: Home is where the heart is.

phrase: (A) hungry belly has no ears.
